Applied AI Scientist — Agentic Decision Systems
   

  

**Location:** 
 Canada or United States (US time zones)
   

  

**Experience:** 
 Typically 2\+ years of relevant applied work, although we care substantially more about the quality and difficulty of the problems you have solved than the number of years you have been solving them.
   

  

**About The Role**
 We are looking for exceptional quantitative thinkers to build
 **agentic systems that help people make better decisions** 
 .
   

  

 This is not primarily a conventional data science role, an LLM application\-development role, or a prompt\-engineering role. We are interested in people who want to understand how intelligent systems can reason over complex problems, use tools and models effectively, learn from evidence, and become systematically better over time.
   

  

**A Central Question In This Role Is**
**How do we make an agentic system measurably better at the decisions it is intended to support?**
 That means moving beyond intuition, demos and prompt alchemy. You will think about objectives, observability, feedback, evaluation datasets, statistical uncertainty, experiments, simulation, failure modes and improvement loops. You should be interested not only in building agents, but in developing rigorous ways for those agents—and the systems around them—to improve.
   

  

 You will work on ambiguous, consequential enterprise problems where the answer is rarely “use an LLM.” Sometimes the right solution will involve an agent. Sometimes it will involve statistical modelling, optimization, machine learning, simulation, rules, or a surprisingly simple piece of mathematics. Frequently it will involve several of these working together.
   

  

 We want people who are technically ambitious, intellectually demanding, empirically minded and impatient with hand\-waving.
   

  

 What You Will Do
   

  

* Design and build agentic decision\-support systems that can reason over data, interact with tools and models, maintain state, decompose complex problems and support consequential human decisions.
* Develop mechanisms for systematic improvement. Design evaluation frameworks, feedback loops, benchmarks, experiments and instrumentation that allow us to determine where a system fails, why it fails and whether a proposed change genuinely improves it.
* Turn “make the agent better” into a quantitative problem. Define measurable objectives and failure modes; build representative test sets; analyze performance distributions rather than anecdotes; and distinguish real improvement from movement on a convenient metric.
* Explore self\-improving agentic architectures. This may involve reflection and critique, adaptive tool or model selection, memory, search, planning, generated training/evaluation data, policy improvement, human feedback, simulation or other mechanisms. We are interested in what works—not in allegiance to a particular architecture.
* Bring statistical and machine\-learning judgment to agentic systems. Use probabilistic modelling, statistical inference, ML, optimization or causal reasoning when they make the system more useful, more reliable or easier to improve.
* Generate high\-quality software using AI coding systems. We expect you to work AI\-natively. The objective is not to demonstrate how quickly you can type Python; it is to produce excellent software.
* Own difficult problems end to end. Work from an initially ambiguous business or decision problem through problem formulation, system design, implementation, evaluation and deployment.
* Challenge the problem definition. A technically sophisticated solution to the wrong problem is still the wrong solution. You should be comfortable questioning assumptions and reframing what is being optimized.
* Work directly with senior technical and business stakeholders. Explain complex ideas precisely without hiding behind jargon, and make uncertainty, assumptions and limitations explicit.


 What We Are Looking For
   

  

 Exceptional quantitative foundations
   

  

 You have rigorous training in a highly quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, statistics, engineering, econometrics, operations research or another discipline involving substantial mathematical and quantitative reasoning.
   

  

 A master's or PhD is welcome, but neither is a substitute for evidence of unusually strong analytical thinking. Exceptional candidates with a bachelor's degree are equally of interest.
   

  

 You should be comfortable reasoning mathematically about unfamiliar problems rather than relying solely on methods you have used before.
   

  

 Experience with agentic systems
   

  

 You have meaningful hands\-on experience designing or developing agentic systems.
   

  

 We are particularly interested in experience involving some combination of:
   

  

* multi\-step reasoning and planning;
* structured outputs and stateful workflows;
* memory and context management;
* multi\-agent or decomposed\-agent architectures;
* agent evaluation;
* automated critique or refinement;
* feedback\-driven adaptation;
* decision\-support applications; and
* mechanisms intended to improve system performance over repeated iterations.


 A chatbot with a system prompt is not, for our purposes, substantial experience building an agentic system. Neither is wrapping an LLM around a vector database and calling the result an agent.
   

  

 Statistical and machine\-learning literacy
   

  

 You do not need to be a specialist in every branch of machine learning, but you should have enough statistical maturity to reason properly about evidence.
   

  

 We expect practical familiarity with statistical modelling and machine learning and, more importantly, sound instincts around:
   

  

* uncertainty;
* validation;
* sampling and selection effects;
* overfitting;
* experiment design;
* measurement;
* predictive versus causal claims;
* distribution shift; and
* determining whether a system actually works.


 You should instinctively ask what the comparison is, how performance is being measured, whether the evaluation resembles the real problem, and how confident we should be in the result.
   

  

 AI\-native software engineering
   

  

 You are extremely effective at producing software, but we do
 **not** 
 equate software engineering ability with manually writing large quantities of code.
   

  

 We expect you to use state\-of\-the\-art coding agents extensively—potentially for essentially all implementations.
   

  

 What matters is whether you can make those systems produce
 **excellent code** 
 .
   

  

**You Should Be Capable Of**
* designing a coherent software architecture before or while implementation emerges;
* decomposing work effectively for coding agents;
* inspecting and interrogating unfamiliar generated code;
* identifying bad abstractions, subtle bugs and unnecessary complexity;
* designing meaningful tests rather than merely achieving test coverage;
* maintaining reproducible environments;
* understanding APIs, data pipelines and production system boundaries;
* debugging systems whose implementation you did not personally type; and
* leaving behind code that another strong engineer can understand, extend and trust.


 You are accountable for every line you ship even if you personally typed none of them.
   

  

 The Intellectual Style We Value
   

  

 The strongest candidates for this role tend to have several things in common.
   

  

 They are deeply curious but difficult to impress. They enjoy abstraction, but they want abstractions to survive contact with data. They are happy to propose an ambitious architecture and equally happy to discard it when a simpler system performs better. They distinguish a compelling demonstration from convincing evidence. They are interested in why something works, where it stops working, and what experiment would distinguish competing explanations. They are willing to use LLMs aggressively without anthropomorphizing them or treating their behavior as magic. And when someone says, “This version feels better,” their instinct is to ask:
 **“Better according to what measurement?”**
 You Will Probably Not Enjoy This Role If
   

  

* Most of your interest is in conventional analytics, dashboards or notebook\-based data science.
* Your experience with generative AI is primarily prompting, chatbot development or basic RAG applications.
* You prefer selecting an AI framework and following its abstractions to thinking from first principles about the underlying system.
* You regard agent behaviour as too unpredictable to evaluate quantitatively or you are satisfied with qualitative demonstrations when controlled measurement is possible.
* You believe increasingly elaborate agent architectures are inherently more intelligent.
* You enjoy writing code but are uncomfortable delegating implementation to AI systems.
* Conversely, you use AI\-generated code without wanting to understand its architecture, test its assumptions or take responsibility for its quality.
* You need requirements to be fully specified before you can make progress.


 Particularly Interesting, But Not Required
   

  

 Experience with one or more of the following would be especially valuable:
   

  

* decision science, causal inference, Bayesian modelling or optimization;
* reinforcement learning, contextual bandits, simulation or adaptive experimentation;
* agent evaluation, observability, benchmark construction or synthetic task generation;
* inference\-time search, test\-time computation, model routing or ensemble systems;
* human\-in\-the\-loop or production agent architectures; and
* complex enterprise decision environments such as financial services, insurance, supply chain or logistics.


 The role is product\-oriented: you will shape the capabilities, workflows and evaluation systems that make our agentic products more useful, reliable and improvable.
   

  

 You will turn difficult enterprise problems, user needs and client lessons into reusable product capabilities. Working with technical, product, domain and client\-facing teams, you will identify high\-leverage problems, formulate improvement hypotheses, and design experiments that distinguish genuine progress from superficial gains.
   

  

 We expect you to move quickly from ideas to prototypes and measurable evidence without compromising reasoning, quality or technical integrity. The goal is not to build the most elaborate AI system, but products that
 **make better decisions, whose performance we can understand, and which we know how to improve.**

 The problems are high\-stakes, data\-dense, and unforgiving.
   

  

 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

**Job Description**
 AI Engineer – Marketing Intelligence \& Automation
   

  

 SS\&C Intralinks \| Marketing – Digital \& Intelligence
   

  

**About The Role**
 SS\&C Intralinks is building an AI\-enabled marketing intelligence model that connects data, digital experiences, automation, and AI to improve how Marketing understands customers, makes decisions, and activates across the funnel. We are hiring an AI Engineer to help build the technical foundation behind that model.
   

  

 This role sits at the intersection of AI engineering, marketing technology, data engineering, and digital experience. You will design and deploy the agents, integrations, data pipelines, orchestration workflows, and intelligence services that turn fragmented marketing data and manual processes into connected, scalable systems.
   

  

 This is not a traditional campaign execution role. You will build the engineering layer beneath an increasingly AI\-enabled marketing organization: connecting platforms and data, enabling agents to reason over trusted information, automating workflows, and creating reusable services that can support personalization, attribution, predictive intent, conversational experiences, content operations, and executive intelligence.
   

  

 You will partner closely with Digital Marketing, Marketing Operations, Demand Generation, Field Marketing, Content/Creative, Analytics, IT, Data, and other stakeholders. The initial focus is establishing a strong architecture and reusable foundation; over time, the role will help operationalize increasingly autonomous marketing capabilities.
   

  

 What You’ll Build
   

  

* AI agents and agentic workflows: Design, build, evaluate, and maintain AI agents that can retrieve trusted marketing and business context, analyze information, recommend actions, and execute approved workflows across marketing systems.
* Marketing intelligence infrastructure: Build the services and pipelines that unify first\-party marketing and CRM data, website behavior, campaign performance, search/AI visibility, intent signals, attribution inputs, and other relevant sources into an accessible intelligence layer.
* API and platform integrations: Connect marketing, data, CMS, CRM, analytics, AI, and workflow platforms through secure APIs, event\-driven integrations, and reusable services rather than brittle one\-off automations.
* Retrieval and knowledge systems: Create RAG and related retrieval patterns that allow AI systems to work from approved messaging, product information, campaign assets, customer insights, brand standards, and other governed enterprise knowledge.
* Predictive and next\-best\-action capabilities: Help develop models and decisioning services that combine first\-party behavior and third\-party signals to identify in\-market accounts, prioritize opportunities, and recommend appropriate next actions.
* Digital journey orchestration: Build the technical capabilities required for adaptive website and digital experiences, including profile\- and account\-aware messaging, content recommendations, calls\-to\-action, and journey logic.
* Conversational AI: Develop LLM\-powered experiences that can engage and qualify visitors, answer questions using approved enterprise knowledge, route inquiries, and integrate with downstream sales and marketing workflows.
* Measurement, attribution, and forecasting: Engineer data and AI services that improve multi\-touch measurement, channel contribution analysis, pipeline intelligence, forecasting, and executive decision support.
* Content and publishing automation: Build systems that connect AI\-assisted content creation, governance, CMS workflows, structured data, localization/personalization, and distribution while maintaining human review where required.
* Search and AI visibility automation: Support SEO/AEO/GEO systems that monitor traditional and AI search visibility, structured data, content performance, citations, and opportunities for optimization at scale.
* Experimentation and evaluation: Create test harnesses, observability, quality controls, and evaluation frameworks for prompts, agents, models, workflows, and digital experiences so deployments are measurable and reliable.
* Reusable engineering standards: Codify successful patterns into components, templates, documentation, and playbooks that allow the broader Marketing organization to scale AI safely and consistently.


 How This Role Supports the Marketing Roadmap
   

  

 The AI Engineer will provide a shared technical foundation for several planned Marketing 4\.0 capabilities. The role is not expected to own each business program independently; instead, it will build the architecture, services, integrations, and AI components that make these capabilities possible.
   

  

* AI\-driven journey orchestration and website personalization
* Hyper\-personalized event and account intelligence
* AI\-driven multi\-touch attribution and forecasting
* Predictive intent and next\-best\-action routing
* Conversational AI and increasingly autonomous inbound qualification
* Content personalization and production systems at scale


 What Success Looks Like
   

  

* Marketing data and knowledge can be accessed by AI systems through governed, well\-documented interfaces rather than manual exports and disconnected point solutions.
* High\-value workflows move from manual execution to reliable human\-in\-the\-loop or autonomous orchestration where appropriate.
* Agents produce traceable, measurable outputs grounded in trusted enterprise data and content.
* Digital, campaign, search, intent, attribution, and pipeline signals can be connected to produce actionable intelligence rather than isolated reporting.
* New AI use cases can be deployed faster because core components—identity, retrieval, integrations, evaluation, observability, permissions, and orchestration—are reusable.
* Marketing teams spend less time assembling data and executing repetitive processes and more time interpreting insights, making decisions, and improving customer experiences.


 Who You Are
   

  

* 4\+ years of experience in AI engineering, software engineering, data engineering, ML engineering, marketing engineering, or a similar role building production technical systems.
* Strong programming skills in Python and experience with JavaScript/TypeScript or another modern application language.
* Hands\-on experience building with LLMs, including APIs, tool/function calling, structured outputs, prompt design, agent frameworks, and production evaluation.
* Experience designing RAG or enterprise knowledge\-retrieval systems, including embeddings, vector search, metadata, chunking, permissions, and source grounding.
* Experience building data pipelines, APIs, event\-driven integrations, and workflow automations across SaaS and enterprise platforms.
* Working knowledge of cloud architecture and data platforms; experience with AWS and Amazon Redshift is particularly relevant.
* Understanding of data modeling, identity resolution, data quality, observability, security, access controls, and governance.
* Experience with marketing technology, CRM, CMS, analytics, digital experience, or marketing automation platforms is strongly preferred.
* Systems thinker who favors durable architecture and reusable services over isolated scripts or one\-off solutions.
* Able to translate ambiguous business problems into technical designs, prototypes, production systems, and measurable outcomes.
* Clear communicator who can explain architecture, tradeoffs, risk, and business impact to both technical and non\-technical partners.
* Comfortable testing emerging AI capabilities while applying appropriate controls for accuracy, privacy, security, and brand risk.
* Experience in B2B, enterprise software, financial technology, or regulated environments is a plus.


 Technical Experience We Value
   

  

* Python; JavaScript/TypeScript; REST/GraphQL APIs; webhooks and event\-driven integration patterns
* LLM APIs and agent frameworks; RAG; vector databases/search; model and prompt evaluation; observability
* AWS services and cloud\-native application patterns; Amazon Redshift; SQL and modern data transformation/orchestration approaches
* CRM and marketing automation integrations, CMS/publishing APIs, web analytics, and customer/digital data sources
* Git\-based development, CI/CD, testing, logging, secrets management, role\-based access, and production monitoring
* Structured data and metadata frameworks such as schema.org/JSON\-LD are useful for digital/search\-oriented use cases


 Operating Principles
   

  

* Build the intelligence layer, not another silo. Solutions should connect and strengthen the broader marketing ecosystem.
* Ground AI in trusted information. Accuracy, provenance, permissions, and data quality matter as much as model capability.
* Automate with intent. Use autonomy where it creates measurable value; retain human review where judgment, compliance, or brand risk requires it.
* Design for reuse. A successful solution should make the next use case easier to build.
* Measure everything. Agents and automations should have clear success criteria, telemetry, and feedback loops.
* Business outcomes over AI novelty. Technology choices should improve decision quality, customer experience, speed, efficiency, or revenue impact.


 Why This Role Matters
   

  

 Marketing is moving from a collection of channels and tools toward a connected intelligence system. This role will help create the engineering foundation that allows SS\&C Intralinks Marketing to use AI across measurement, digital experiences, content, demand generation, field marketing, and full\-funnel engagement—without creating a new set of disconnected AI point solutions.
